subject: Concord Systems - Dedicated GPU SKU strategy and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22 09:12 -0700
Subject: Concord Systems - SKU framing for Dedicated proposal (early thoughts)

Team —

Following yesterday's call with Concord (Sara + Mike), I've sketched a draft SKU strategy tied to their workload profile. Their ask: predictable latency at 99th percentile for interactive search/chat plus a smaller set of long-context summarization and batch embedding pipelines. Key constraints: 1) peak concurrent sessions ~1.2k, 2) spikes (x3) during reporting windows, 3) strict data residency in us-west.

High level recommendation (first pass):
- Primary: mix H100 (compute-heavy, long-context models) + L4 nodes for chat/concurrency.
- Safety net: A100 40GB class as the fallback for memory-bound variants and for graceful degradation when H100 capacity is constrained.

Rationale bullets:
- H100: best throughput per-slot for FP16/TF32 large-context decoders; minimizes tokens/sec cost for long-context summarization and high batch throughput.
- A100 (40GB): better single-device memory for models that don't quantize well or require large KV caches; useful for fragmented model splits and for customer models we can't quantize below 8-bit.
- L4: cost-efficient, high-concurrency node for chat-like workloads where model size and context are modest; helps keep unit economics sane for interactive queries.

Operational notes to consider: prefix/KV caching to reduce H100 load for repeated session prefixes; tiling/sequence-slicing for the longest jobs; a simple routing policy that pins premium traffic to H100 and routes best-effort chat to L4 with A100 used as the mid-tier fallback.

Attached: concord-sku-sensitivity.xlsx (sensitivity matrix I started) and a one-pager I will clean up.

Ask: please review and flag major missed assumptions by EOD. Karthik — I want an ops feasibility note. Dylan — can you sanity-check the concurrency split and rough token/sec mapping? Irene / Dev — anything missing from procurement/infra constraints?

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Concord Systems - SKU framing for Dedicated proposal (early thoughts)

Naomi — good framing. A few quick points from capacity modeling: 

- Concurrency split: if we assume 70% chat (short context <= 2k tokens) and 30% long-context jobs (>= 16k tokens) during normal ops, L4s can handle ~5-8x more short-chat sessions per slot than H100 given identical latency targets. That gives us cost leverage.
- H100 sizing: for the longest summarization pipelines (16k-32k prefixed contexts), H100 yields ~2.5-3x throughput improvement over A100 on batch FP16 kernel stack; that materially reduces slot count for those jobs.
- A100 role: instead of pure fallback, propose a small pool of A100-40GB reserved for models that currently fail 8-bit quantization (we've seen 12-15% quality delta for some customer weights). Use as a gradient: cold fallback -> spill to A100 -> degrade to reduced context if needed.

Small operational ask: include an eviction policy for interactive sessions in the design doc (e.g., LRU based on session idle time) so we can bound memory fragmentation on L4.

I'll attach a short table to the XLS with concurrency ratios — will send in a minute.

—Dylan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22 12:26 -0700
Subject: Re: Concord Systems - SKU framing for Dedicated proposal (early thoughts)

Thanks Naomi / Dylan — adding ops/finance perspective.

- Cost arithmetic (ballpark): H100 slot (reserved) ~ $Xk/month effective (depends on iso occupancy); A100-40GB slot slightly cheaper but needs more slots for the same throughput on long workloads. L4 slot is ~20-30% of H100 cost for chat workloads. I'll put exact figures in the sensitivity sheet.
- Quantization: we should plan for a two-track model onboarding: 
  1) Aggressive quantization (8-bit/LLM.int8) on L4 for chat variants — typical quality delta small for conversation models.
  2) Conservative path on H100/A100 for generation-heavy long-context models (keep fp16 or bf16).
- Recommendation on capacity buffer: reserve 25% burst headroom for scheduled reporting windows; add an autoscale policy that can borrow from cross-region burst pool if us-west saturates.

Procurement note (Irene / Dev): Concord may ask for simplified SKU pricing and a clear escape hatch if usage doesn't reach projected run-rate in Q1. Consider a stepped-commit (month 1 pilot, month 2 committed baseline, month 3 ramp).

I'll annotate the spreadsheet with per-sku latency and tokens/sec numbers and scenarios for 50th/99th percentiles.

Karthik
VP, Solutions

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@concordsys.com>, Mike Ellis <mike.ellis@concordsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@concordsys.com
Date: 2026-10-23 09:08 -0700
Subject: Concord Systems - Recommended Dedicated SKU mix and next steps (PoC + MAP)

Sara / Mike —

Thanks again for the call. We've run the initial sizing and have a recommended Dedicated SKU mix that balances 99th percentile latency targets with predictable unit costs. Summary: 

Recommended architecture (pilot -> committed):
- Pilot (30 days): small H100 pool (2 slots) + L4 cluster sized for expected chat concurrency (~120 L4 slots) + 1 A100-40GB hot-standby node. Purpose: validate routing, KV caching, and estimate real token/sec.
- Committed baseline (Q1 target): H100 fleet (8 slots) for long-context summarization + L4 pool (360 slots) for chat + A100 pool (4 slots) for memory-heavy fallbacks and migration windows.

Important tradeoffs: 
- Memory vs latency: H100 gives better throughput on long-context models (lower tokens/sec cost) but is costlier per slot. A100 is pragmatic when a model's KV cache or embedding tables exceed L4/A100 quantization constraints. L4 should be the workhorse for low-latency conversational paths.
- Quality controls: we'll onboard models through a two-track eval — aggressive quantized variants for chat (L4) and unquantized/FP16 on H100/A100 where quality matters.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — high level:
1) Week 0–2: PoC setup (pilot fleet + routing rules).
2) Week 2–4: telemetry collection (latency p50/p99, tokens/sec, cache hit-rate).
3) Week 4–6: tune batching/tiling parameters and finalize SKU commit.
4) Week 6+: place reserve commit and move to reserved billing.

Attachments: concord-sku-sensitivity.xlsx (capacity & cost scenarios) and concord-map-poa.pdf (MAP with dates). Drive folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-concord-poc

Open items for Concord to confirm: preferred pilot start week, acceptable pilot SLA window for p99 latency, and procurement contact for a stepped-commit.

If this looks good, we can produce a short SOW + pricing appendix for procurement.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
